(4) 66.5% of US ES-SCLC patients starting first-line platinum received it with a PD-(L)1 antibody, 1,711 of 2,573 (Sankar et al., Adv Ther 2025;43:214-230, doi:10.1007/s12325-025-03408-z, Flatiron 2018 to 2023). (5) 73% of patients starting chemo-immunotherapy induction finished it without progression and entered maintenance, 483 of 660 (IMforte, Paz-Ares et al., Lancet 2025;405:2129-2143, doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01011-6). 0.118 x 0.709 x 0.9206 x 0.665 x 0.7318 = 0.0375, about 8,500 patients a year
column12: DeLLphi-305 enrols after 3 to 4 cycles of platinum, etoposide and durvalumab without progression, which is this population. Three things are not taken off: induction on atezolizumab rather than durvalumab (no US split found), ECOG 0 to 1, and the NCDB's own exclusions, which make its 92% an upper bound. Sankar's 66.5% averages 2018, before first-line immunotherapy was approved, so it leans low today. The IMforte share is a trial cohort's

column11: a judgement. The case for: tarlatamab is the only agent with an overall survival win in second-line SCLC (DeLLphi-304 HR 0.60, median 13.6 against 8.3 months, Mountzios et al., N Engl J Med 2025), and Amgen is already moving it forward. The case against: the maintenance slot has an approved incumbent, Zepzelca with atezolizumab since October 2025 (Jazz Q2 2026 10-Q 0001232524-26-000045, on IMforte: OS HR 0.73), DeLLphi-305's own control arm is durvalumab maintenance, and the label would carry cytokine release syndrome monitoring and step-up dosing that a maintenance patient in remission does not otherwise need
